mainTopic: When a capital or כרת sin and a money debt come together: רב חסדא on stolen חלב, רבי אבין's arrow, and the purse stolen on שבת
overview: The amud asks when one act brings both a death-penalty or כרת sin and a money debt, and the person is freed from paying. It begins with the end of רבי אבין's case: an arrow shot four אמות on שבת tore someone's silk as it flew. רב חסדא says even רבי נחוניא בן הקנה agrees that a thief who steals and eats חלב must pay, because the theft came before the eating. The גמרא asks whether this argues with רבי אבין, who exempts the arrow-shooter because lifting and placing are one act. It answers that the cases differ in two ways: eating can happen without lifting, and the fat can be put back while the arrow cannot. The two reasons give different rulings for a man carrying a knife who tears silk on the way. Then רב ביבי בר אביי challenges רבי אבין from a ברייתא that makes a purse thief pay on שבת. The גמרא first says the thief lifted the purse to hide it. רבי יוחנן's rule rules that out, so the גמרא says instead that he lifted it to carry it out but stopped. It narrows this to stopping to rest, and then asks what the law is if he only stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder, a question taken up on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the arrow-and-silk case
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an earlier case about an arrow shot on שבת that tore someone's silk as it flew.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of an earlier question, which began before this section. Someone shot an arrow on שבת, and on its way it tore another person's silk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the שבת sin, which carries the death penalty, frees him from paying for the silk. The silk tore while the שבת sin was still in progress, before the arrow landed. רבי אבין's answer to this case will be quoted in the next steps.

Tore or ripped

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tail end of a case that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person is exempt from paying for damage done at the same moment as a death-penalty שבת sin.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the thief who eats stolen חלב must pay
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that even רבי נחוניא בן הקנה agrees that someone who steals and eats his friend's חלב must pay, because the theft came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב חסדא said: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה agrees that if someone steals his friend's חלב and eats it, he must pay. He already became liable for theft before he reached the sin of eating חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement mentioned earlier and looks at it closely. רב חסדא says the thief must pay for the חלב he stole and ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה holds that a כרת sin frees a person from paying money, just like a death-penalty sin. Here, though, the sin and the debt are not at the same moment. The theft happened when he picked up the fat, and eating it came later, so the debt was already locked in.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself; the גמרא now analyzes a statement it mentioned earlier
Forbidden fat, which carries כָּרֵת for eating it
Agrees or concedes, even though he usually holds otherwise
Became liable for theft

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main principle of the סוגיא: you are exempt from paying only when the money debt and the serious sin happen at the same moment.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Chisda said:
Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana agrees
phrases.notes: His view, from earlier, is that a כרת sin frees you from paying, the same way a death-penalty sin does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the arrow case for now and goes back to analyze רב חסדא's statement directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief who steals and eats חלב must pay, because the theft came before the כרת sin. This holds even according to רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא argue with רבי אבין's arrow ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב חסדא argues with רבי אבין. רבי אבין exempts the arrow-shooter because lifting and placing are one act, so lifting the חלב should count as part of eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רב חסדא argues with רבי אבין? רבי אבין said: if someone shoots an arrow on שבת from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות, and on its way it tears silk, he is exempt from paying. Lifting is done for the sake of placing. Here too, lifting the fat is done for the sake of eating it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא by quoting רבי אבין's ruling on the arrow. That ruling seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silk tore before the arrow landed, yet רבי אבין still exempts the shooter. That is because the lifting at the start is part of one single שבת act that ends with the placing. By the same logic, picking up the חלב should be part of the one act of eating it, so the theft and the כרת sin would happen at the same moment and he should not have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say he disagrees? A way the גמרא suggests that two rabbis argue
Lifting an object from its place; the first half of carrying on שבת
Setting an object down; the second half of carrying on שבת
Picking something up; this is how a thief acquires a stolen item
Four cubits; moving an object this far in רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים is forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: Shall we say he disagrees with Rabbi Avin?
For Rabbi Avin said:
One who shoots an arrow
from the start of four (cubits) to the end of four,
phrases.notes: He means on שבת in the public domain, where moving something four cubits is a death-penalty sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling from step 2 using רבי אבין's ruling on the arrow case from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the theft is a separate, earlier moment from the eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first stage of an act counts as part of its last stage (arrow: lifting is part of placing), then lifting the חלב is part of eating it. The theft would then happen at the same moment as the כרת sin, and he should be exempt from paying.

steps.title: First difference: placing needs lifting, but eating does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. You cannot place without lifting, but you can eat without lifting by bending down.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, placing is impossible without lifting. Here, eating is possible without lifting, because if he wants he can bend down and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge and says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying on שבת always needs both lifting and placing, so the two halves are one act. Eating does not need lifting at all, since you can bend down to the food. So lifting the חלב is a separate act of theft that came before the eating, and רב חסדא does not argue with רבי אבין.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?! The גמרא uses this to say the comparison does not work
It is impossible
He bends down and eats

phrases.english: How can you compare?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַנָּחָה בְּלֹא עֲקִירָה.
phrases.english: There, placing is impossible without lifting.
Here, eating is possible without lifting,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the arrow case and the חלב case. It does not reject either ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Lifting is required for placing, but it is not required for eating, so lifting the חלב is a separate act.

steps.title: Second difference: the arrow cannot be taken back, but the fat can
steps.stepSummary: Another way to tell the cases apart: once the arrow is shot it cannot be brought back, but the thief could put the fat back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another answer: there, if he wants to bring the arrow back, he cannot. Here, he can put the fat back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why the arrow case and the fat case are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the arrow leaves the bow, the placing is sure to happen, so lifting and placing are locked together as one act. After lifting the fat, the thief could still change his mind and put it back. So the theft stands on its own before the eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; introduces a second answer
To bring it back
He is able to bring it back

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the arrow case is different. (1) Placing can never happen without lifting, but eating can happen without lifting. (2) The arrow cannot be called back, but the fat can be put back.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
there, if he wants to bring it back,
he cannot bring it back.
Here, he can bring it back.
phrases.notes: The thief could put the stolen fat back after picking it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent way to reject the comparison from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the arrow case and the חלב case for a different reason than step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The arrow's flight cannot be stopped, but the lifting of the fat can still be undone, so the theft is separate from the eating.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two answers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons it just gave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between this version and that version?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two answers would lead to different rulings. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers agree on the arrow and the fat. The גמרא wants a case where one reason says 'one act' and the other says 'separate acts.'

steps.title: The knife case: where the two answers split
steps.stepSummary: Someone carrying a knife through רשות הרבים who tears silk on the way. Under the first answer it is one act and he is exempt; under the second he could stop, so he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is someone who carries a knife through רשות הרבים and tears silk as he walks. According to the version that says placing is impossible without lifting, here too placing is impossible without lifting. According to the version that says he cannot bring it back, here he can bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case where the two answers lead to different rulings: carrying a knife by hand on שבת and tearing silk with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first reason, carrying the knife still needs both lifting and placing, so it is one act and he is exempt from paying for the silk. By the second reason, a person walking with a knife can stop or turn back at any time, unlike an arrow. So the lifting is not locked to the placing, and he must pay for the silk.

Knife
Public domain, where carrying is forbidden on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: In the knife case, the first answer (placing needs lifting) means he is exempt from paying for the silk. The second answer (he could take it back) means he must pay.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Carrying a knife by hand and tearing silk on the way: the first answer says he is exempt from paying, and the second says he must pay.

steps.title: Returning to רבי אבין's arrow rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי אבין's statement so it can examine it on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now let's look at the statement itself. רבי אבין said: If someone shoots an arrow on שבת from the start of four אמות to the end of four אמות, and on the way it tears silk, he does not pay for the silk. This is because lifting is needed for placing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It quotes רבי אבין's rule again so it can test it against a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שבת violation is only finished when the arrow lands four אמות away. But רבי אבין counts the whole flight, from the shot to the landing, as one act. So the tearing of the silk happens during the act that carries the death penalty, and he is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. The גמרא returns to look at a statement it quoted earlier.
Lifting an object from its place, the first part of carrying on שבת
Setting the object down, the last part of carrying
Silk cloth

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Avin said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is coming back to the statement it quoted back in step 3, to look at it properly.

phrases.english: One who shoots an arrow
from the beginning of four amos to the end of four amos

is exempt (from paying),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source of רבי אבין's rule after the side discussion about רב חסדא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damage done between the lifting and the landing counts as part of the שבת act, so the person does not pay.

steps.title: רב ביבי quotes a ברייתא about stealing a purse on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a thief who lifts a purse must pay, but a thief who drags it out does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי objected using a ברייתא: Someone who steals a purse on שבת must pay. He already became liable for the theft before he reached the שבת violation that carries סקילה. But if he dragged the purse along the ground straight out of the house, he does not pay. In that case the שבת violation and the theft happen at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי אבין. This step quotes the source, and the next step will show exactly where the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the purse makes it his, so the theft is already done. Only later, when he carries it out, does the שבת violation begin, so he pays. Dragging is different: the purse only becomes his when it leaves the house, which is the same moment as the שבת violation, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A purse
Death by stoning, the punishment for breaking שבת on purpose
Dragging along the ground without lifting

steps.confusionAlert: Dragging does not count as lifting. So when he drags the purse, the theft only happens when it leaves the house, at the same moment as the שבת violation.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye raised an objection:
One who steals a purse on Shabbat
is liable (to pay),
because he already became liable for the theft
before he came to the prohibition punished by stoning.
If he was dragging it out, dragging it out,
he is exempt,
since the Shabbat prohibition and the theft
come at the same moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to go against רבי אבין
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's rule that lifting is part of placing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the lifting as a separate theft that comes before the שבת violation. That is not how רבי אבין sees lifting.

steps.title: The challenge: lifting should be part of carrying out
steps.stepSummary: If lifting is part of the act, the purse thief should be exempt, just like the arrow-shooter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why does he pay? Here too, let us say that lifting is a necessary part of carrying out!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch of רב ביבי's challenge. By רבי אבין's logic, lifting the purse should count as part of the שבת act, so the thief should not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lifting and placing are one act, then the theft happens at the same time as the שבת violation. In that case the thief should be exempt, just like the one who drags the purse. The ברייתא says he pays, so it seems to go against רבי אבין.

keyTerms.meaning: But why?
Lifting up
Carrying an object from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: But why (is he liable)?
Here too, let us say:
lifting is a necessary part of carrying out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the contradiction between the ברייתא in step 9 and רבי אבין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If lifting were part of the act, the ברייתא would exempt the thief. It makes him pay, so lifting must be a separate step.

steps.title: He lifted it only to hide it, then changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a thief who first lifted the purse to hide it in the house, and only later decided to take it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? He lifted the purse in order to hide it inside the house. Then he changed his mind and carried it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבין. It explains that in the ברייתא, the lifting was never meant for carrying out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting counts as part of carrying only when he lifts in order to carry. Here he lifted it to hide it, so the lifting was a separate act. That lifting completed the theft before any שבת violation.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow down a source to a specific case.
To hide it away
Changed his mind

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
Where he lifted it in order to hide it,
and he changed his mind about it and carried it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that any lifting is separate from carrying out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about lifting done for a different purpose, so it does not go against רבי אבין.

steps.title: If he changed his mind, there is no שבת violation at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone lifted an object for a different purpose and then took it out, he is exempt for שבת. So the ברייתא could not be talking about this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case like this, is he even liable for שבת? But רב סימון said that רבי אמי said that רבי יוחנן said: Someone who moves items from one corner of his house to another, and then changes his mind and carries them out, is exempt. This is because the lifting was not done for this purpose from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings רבי יוחנן to show that a person who changed his mind is not liable for שבת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says he pays because the theft came before the stoning offense. That assumes he did commit a stoning offense. But by רבי יוחנן, someone who lifted for another purpose does not break שבת at all. So the ברייתא's wording does not fit this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Moves or clears items away
A corner
From the very start

phrases.english: And in a case like this, is he liable?
phrases.notes: He means liable for שבת, which is what the stoning in the ברייתא is about.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Simon say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who moves items from corner to corner,
and changed his mind about them and carried them out
is exempt,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי חַיָּיב? וְהָאָמַר רַב סִימוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that he lifted the purse to hide it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי יוחנן, changing your mind after lifting removes the שבת liability. But the ברייתא assumes there is a stoning offense.

steps.title: He lifted it to carry it out, but he stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its answer: he lifted the purse to carry it out, but stopped inside before leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say he lifted it in order to hide it. Instead say he lifted it in order to carry it out. And what case are we dealing with here? Where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes its answer. The thief did plan to carry the purse out, but he stopped inside the house on the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His plan to carry it out makes him liable for שבת, so רבי יוחנן's rule does not apply. Stopping on the way breaks the link between the lifting and the carrying out, so the lifting stands alone as theft. The arrow is different, because once it is shot it cannot stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that. Used to change a reading or an earlier answer.
When he stopped

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבין stands. Lifting counts as part of the act when it flows straight into the placing, like an arrow in flight. If the thief makes a real stop in the middle, the theft is complete before the שבת violation, so he must pay. Steps 14-15 explain which kind of stop counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether a person pays for damage done during a capital act depends on one thing: are the two parts of the act joined without a break?

phrases.english: Do not say "in order to hide it,"
rather say "in order to carry it out,"
and with what case are we dealing here?
Where he stopped.
phrases.notes: He stopped inside, before taking the purse out to רשות הרבים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא עַל מְנָת לְהַצְנִיעוֹ, אֶלָּא אֵימָא עַל מְנָת לְהוֹצִיאוֹ

steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the earlier answer and limiting the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He lifted it to hide it. That would remove the שבת liability entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: He lifted it to carry it out, so he is liable for שבת. But he stopped, which separates the theft from the carrying out, so he pays.

steps.title: Why did the thief stop?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the thief stopped. It rejects the idea that he stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder, because that is just the normal way of carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stopped. For what purpose? If he stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder, that is the normal way of carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the answer from Step 13 by asking what kind of stop the thief made. It shows that one kind of stop cannot be what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 13 needs the stop to cut the act in two, so that the theft is finished before the שבת carrying starts. Stopping to shift a load is a normal part of carrying, so it does not break the act. That kind of stop would leave the thief exempt from paying, which does not fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He stopped (stood still) while still inside
For what purpose?
To adjust or settle the load on his shoulder
That is the normal way (of carrying)

phrases.english: He stopped — for what purpose?
If it was to adjust the load on his shoulder —

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד לְמַאי? אִי לְכַתֵּף אוֹרְחֵיהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from Step 13 by asking exactly what kind of stop the thief made.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the thief's stop, since only a real break between acts would support the answer in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 13 that the thief stopped inside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A stop to adjust the load is part of normal carrying. The act would then be one continuous act, and the thief would still be exempt from paying, like the arrow-shooter.

steps.title: He stopped to rest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is about a thief who stopped to rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he stopped to rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The thief stopped to rest, which is a real break in the carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping to rest ends the first act. When he picks up and walks out again, that is a brand-new act of carrying for שבת. So the theft was already complete before the שבת violation started, and he must pay. This fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier option and giving the correct one)
To rest

steps.whatToRemember: The purse thief must pay because he stopped to rest. That break makes his later walking out a separate act, so the theft happened before the שבת carrying began.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he stopped to rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 by naming the only kind of stop that works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He stopped in order to rest, which breaks the carrying into two separate acts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any stop inside might be enough to separate the theft from the שבת act.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only stopping to rest creates a real break. When he moves on, he starts a new act.

steps.title: What if he stopped only to adjust the load?
steps.stepSummary: Based on the last answer, the גמרא asks what the law would be if the thief stopped only to adjust the load on his shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that comes out of the last answer. The discussion continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was explained as a thief who stopped to rest. That leaves open the case of a thief who only paused to shift the load. The גמרא now wants to know whether that thief pays or is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: But (moving to the case not yet covered)
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: But if he stopped to adjust the load on his shoulder — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the case that Step 15 left out and asks what its law is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the law is for a thief who paused only to adjust the load on his shoulder: is he exempt from paying, or does he pay? The question follows from step 14, which called that kind of stop the normal way of carrying.
